 Cricket-India win toss and bowl in first test against New Zealand
 Thursday, 19 Nov 2026
 | 6:13 AM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 FILE PHOTO: Cricket - International Test Match Series - Fifth Test - England v India - Kia Oval, London, Britain - July 31, 2025 India's Shubman Gill in action Action Images via Reuters/Paul Childs/File Photo 
 Nov 19 (Reuters) - India won the ⁠toss and will bowl first in the first test against New ⁠Zealand in Wellington on Thursday with captain Shubman Gill hoping his four ‌seamers will be able to make early inroads on a grassy deck. 
 • Jasprit Bumrah returns to lead an Indian pace attack featuring Anshul Kamboj, Prasidh Krishna and Akash Deep but there was ​no place for Mohammed Siraj
 • New Zealand captain ⁠Tom Latham confirmed his team on ⁠Wednesday with Devon Conway, Rachin Ravindra and Tom Blundell all returning to the ⁠batting ‌line-up from spells on the sidelines
 • Kyle Jamieson, Matt Henry, Jacob Duffy and all-rounder Nathan Smith also form a four-pronged pace attack
 • "There's a ⁠bit more initially in the wicket as compared to ​the second innings so ‌hopefully we're able to exploit that," said Gill
 • "Very difficult for Siraj and (Gurnoor ⁠Brar) for both ​of them to miss out. They did decently well in the ODI series. Gurnoor, obviously, you know, was man of the series there, so it was a hard decision ⁠for us"
 • "We would have had a bowl first ​as well," said Latham. "But I guess sometimes here at the Basin when it's a nice day, the wicket doesn't look like it's as thick as what it ⁠previously has been the last few years
 • "But regardless of whether you're batting or bowling first, it's about trying to do that first session really well"
 • New Zealand: Tom Latham (captain), Devon Conway, Henry Nicholls, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell, Glenn ​Phillips, Nathan Smith, Kyle Jamieson, Matt Henry, Jacob Duffy
 • ⁠India: KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal, Shubman Gill (captain), Rishabh Pant, Washington Sundar, Dhruv ​Jurel, Anshul Kamboj, Akash Deep, Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh ‌Krishna
 • New Zealand top the World Test ​Championship standings. India are fourth.
 • The second and final test in Christchurch starts on November 27
 (Reporting by Nick Mulvenney, editing by Toby Davis)
